Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Evidence from seven demo pairs

## Confirmed rule from latest recurrence

Task operation: Preserve only the broad, solid foreground rectangular objects (and any pre-existing structured multi-cell objects); erase scattered isolated foreground noise. The relevant rectangles are those that are internally filled as compact blocks, while noisy isolated markers and small local intrusions are removed. Demo evidence for this recurrence: Pair 1 (bg7) repaired two distinct 0 rectangles (rows 0-6, col6-7; rows1-3, cols10-13) and retained 9 rectangle at rows7-8 cols0-4, 8 objects in lower right; cleaned external isolated noise and repaired foreign intrusions. Pair 2 (bg5) removed sparse noise while preserving rectangular 3 objects at rows0-7 cols1-7, 4 blocks at rows1-3 cols10-12 and rows14-17 (two adjacent blocks separated by a column), 2 block rows10-12 cols7-10, and 2 block rows20-21 cols0-1; corrected intrusions. Pair 3 (bg0) only corrected one intrusion in 9 rectangle rows4-9 cols2-6; other background unchanged. Pair 4 (bg9) repaired several 1,6,3,2 blocks and removed sparse noise; preserved object footprints including blocks. Combined with accepted test, the cleanup scope includes solid rectangular objects of multiple colors/dimensions, removes isolated noise, and repairs embedded foreign-color cells to object color; avoid assuming every apparent component gets expanded, and preserve object boundaries exactly.

Operational rule now supported by demos/test: identify foreground rectangular object footprints from repeated/dense regions; for each selected rectangle, restore all its cells to its dominant foreground color. Remove external non-background singletons. Do not extend boundaries, merge neighboring objects, or erase valid rectangles. In tests with ambiguity, request a demo rather than broad deletion: earlier submissions based on removing noise plus filling all candidate shapes, and clearing most of the grid except a few suspected major objects, were rejected.

4. Require a candidate to reproduce every demo cell by cell before applying it.
5. Do not reuse any prior failed guess or accepted test output as a template; this is a task-family reminder, not a solved formula.
6. Return one protocol-compliant JSON action only.
